evidence: The films were evaluated for their crystallinity, morphology and composition using complementary techniques such as grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction (GI-XRD), atomic force microscopy (AFM), Rutherford backscattering (RBS), nuclear-reaction-analysis (NRA) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). UV/Vis spectroscopy of In2O3 films (30 nm) grown on borosilicate glass at 230 °C showed a high degree of optical transparency (>90%) in the visible and NIR ranges and these results (see ESI, Fig. S9 †) are in close agreement with reports for In2O3 films grown by other ALD processes. From ellipsometry measurements, the refractive index was estimated to be 2.08 which is comparable to In2O3 films obtained by rf-sputtering.
